Thanks for the call earlier. Per our discussion I attached a super-rough estimate (snowcap_initial_estimate.csv) mapping a few demand scenarios to Reserved capacity bands. Two quick asks to make the recommendation deterministic:

- Can you confirm the steady-state QPS for embeddings (avg & p95) and the peak hourly QPS? You mentioned a lot of downstream retrieval work, so embeddings cost dominates for embeddings-heavy pipelines.
- For generation: what % of requests need >8k tokens context vs short replies (<=1k tokens)? Long-context runs will push us to H100-class devices.

High-level we see three SKU patterns that map to workload mixes:
- L4-dominant: embeddings-heavy, short responses, cost-focused.
- A100-mixed: balanced embeddings + occasional medium-length generation with large batching.
- H100-first: frequent long-context gen and high memory KV demand.

Ben / Hiro / Karthik —

Forwarding Lisa's sample. Summary observations and what we need from Eng/Solution:
1) Embeddings volume is material (p95 420 QPS, peak 1.2k/hr). Primarily cost-driven; L4 presents a lower-cost option per embedding unit but has lower memory and multi-request throughput characteristics.
2) Gen is low QPS but has a non-trivial tail of very long contexts (~8% >10k tokens). Those requests demand H100-class memory + KV cache headroom.
3) SLOs are strict on embeddings latency (95th <120ms). That suggests colocated L4 with aggressive batching or pinned A100 depending on network hops.

Ask: Hiro / Karthik — can you map these numbers into a two-stage SKU plan (pilot -> reserved commit) that hits cost targets for embeddings while preserving fallthrough for long-gen? Include: recommended fleet mix, pre-warm counts, autoscale buffer %, routing policy (latency-first vs cost-first), and quick estimate of monthly committed cost under a 12-month commit.

I'll prepare the MOP and schedule a 30-min canary walkthrough once we have the sizing.

Subject: Re: Fwd: Snowcap workload — sku mapping + delivery plan (tech note)

Hannah / team —

Attached: redwood_sku_field_notes_h100_a100_l4.pdf (technical notes, 6 pages). Below is the pragmatic plan that balances cost and SLOs given Snowcap's mix:

Recommendation: Hybrid fleet with routing and pre-warmed pools
- L4 pool (embeddings primary): 12 x L4 devices in a dedicated embeddings cluster. Rationale: L4 gives best $/embed at small token lengths; use continuous batching and short-prefetch to meet 95th latency <120ms. Keep per-device batcher tuned to 32-64 micro-batches and aggressive prefix caching for popular embedding prefixes.
- A100 pool (mixed gen + fallback): 6 x A100 (40GB) for medium-length generation and as the fallback for L4 when spike or model mismatch occurs. A100 has better memory and stable throughput at heavier batch sizes; cheaper to reserve than H100.
- H100 pool (long-context gen): 2 x H100 pre-warmed slots for persistent long-context KV sessions (10k+ tokens). These are kept warm and pinned to reduce cold-start KV warm-up penalty. Autoscale policy allows burst to additional H100s in the shared burst pool if needed.

Key config choices:
- Routing policy: embeddings -> L4 preferred; if latency SLA violation predicted (queue depth + estimate), route to A100 automatically. For requests with context >8k tokens, route directly to H100.
- Cache/KV sizing: reserve ~25% of H100 memory for persistent KV per long job; store KV in local fast NVMe cache salted by customer namespace. Estimated per long-job KV reserve: 64GB.
- Autoscale & buffer: maintain 1.5x headroom for embeddings during peak hour (to avoid queuing spikes). For H100 maintain 1 pre-warmed slot per active long-job; for predictable scheduled summarization windows (Snowcap has weekly batch jobs), schedule pre-warm starting 15 minutes before the window.
- Quantization: embeddings model on L4 can run int8/4 quantized for cost; gen models on H100/A100 keep fp16/mixed precision to preserve quality for long contexts.

Cost sketch (monthly committed 12-mo) — rough ballpark:
- 12x L4 reserved + buffer: ~$8k/mo
- 6x A100 reserved: ~$45k/mo
- 2x H100 reserved (plus 1 burst standby on demand): ~$70k/mo
Total committed estimate: ~$123k/mo (very rough). Monthly on-demand for bursts (~20% headroom) add incremental variable cost.

Fallthrough and reliability:
- If L4 pool saturated, route to A100 with degraded per-unit cost; if A100 saturated and request is long-context, queue or reject based on customer-configured SLO policy.
- Canary: run 48h pilot with 2 L4 + 1 A100 + pre-warmed H100 to validate latency numbers and batching settings. We can gather token-level cost and adjust fleet mix.

Next steps for Sales/Mgr: produce a 48h canary MOP with expected telemetry and success criteria (p95 latency, embed unit cost, fallback ratio).
